AtReadTime.description: Text in force at one instant.
AtReadTime.title: AtReadTime

ClaimOccurrence.description: Where a claim occurs in one selected version (D140 §3.4).
ClaimOccurrence.title: ClaimOccurrence

ClaimValidPrecision.description: How narrow an author's stated validity window was (D48).
ClaimValidPrecision.title: ClaimValidPrecision

DeclaredEffectivePeriod.description: One live declaration of a version, exactly as it was declared.
DeclaredEffectivePeriod.title: DeclaredEffectivePeriod

DiscoveryHit.description: Exact wire contract for one query-space search result.
DiscoveryHit.title: _DiscoveryHit

DocumentDeletion.description:
What deleting one document changed in the live memory.

The counts describe this call. A call that finishes a deletion another
path started reports only the work it finished.
DocumentDeletion.title: DocumentDeletion

DocumentPeopleMatch.description: One distinct person an authors/recipients filter matched.
DocumentPeopleMatch.title: DocumentPeopleMatch

DocumentReference.description: One reference, resolved against one source window and target version.
DocumentReference.title: DocumentReference

DocumentReferenceSource.description: The source side of one reference row.
DocumentReferenceSource.title: DocumentReferenceSource

DocumentReferenceTarget.description:
The resolved target side of one reference row.

Only what the row's status allows is set: the lineage for
``target_not_in_force`` and ``pinned_version_unavailable``; the version
and ``applies_during`` for ``target_processing``; the section and its
first chunks for ``resolved``.
DocumentReferenceTarget.title: DocumentReferenceTarget

DocumentReferencesPage.description:
A page of ``document_references`` rows.

Ordered by direction (outgoing first), source document, source version,
reference, window start and target version. ``cursor`` pins
``evaluated_at`` and ``believed_at``; a page may be short when the scan
bound was reached and still carry a cursor. ``too_broad`` is set (and
``rows`` empty) when the section has too many descendant keys.
DocumentReferencesPage.title: DocumentReferencesPage

DocumentReferencesRequest.description:
One ``document_references`` call (D140 §6.2).

Exactly one of ``chunk_id`` (the chunk's version and section are the
source) or ``doc_id`` (with an optional ``section_key``). ``time``
selects source versions; omitted, it is ``current`` — except with a
``chunk_id``, where it is the chunk version's in-force time up to now.
DocumentReferencesRequest.title: DocumentReferencesRequest

DocumentReferencesTooBroad.description: The section resolves to more descendant keys than one call follows.
DocumentReferencesTooBroad.title: DocumentReferencesTooBroad

DocumentSearchFilters.description:
General document metadata filters (D134 §3); every one given must hold.

``authors`` and ``recipients`` match a person when any listed term equals
their normalized address or appears as whole words in their normalized
name (lower case, accents removed): ``"alice"`` matches "Alice Novák".
Date ranges are inclusive and exclude documents that do not declare the
date.
DocumentSearchFilters.title: DocumentSearchFilters

DocumentSearchPerson.description: One author or recipient as the document declares them.
DocumentSearchPerson.title: DocumentSearchPerson

DocumentSearchRequest.description:
One ``search_documents`` call.

With a ``query`` the results are ranked by name and content matches and
there is no cursor. Without one they are every document the filters
match, newest declared creation date first, paged by ``cursor``.
DocumentSearchRequest.title: DocumentSearchRequest

DocumentSearchResult.description: One matching document, described by the version it was judged by.
DocumentSearchResult.title: DocumentSearchResult

EffectiveInterval.description: One in-force interval ``[from, until)``; null bounds are open.
EffectiveInterval.title: EffectiveInterval

EffectivePeriodInput.description:
One declared period during which a version's text is in force (D140).

The period is half-open: ``effective_from`` is included and
``effective_until`` is not. Without ``effective_until`` the period lasts
until the next declared start in the document's lineage, so declaring a
new edition ends its predecessor without touching it.
EffectivePeriodInput.title: EffectivePeriodInput

EffectivePeriodsRequest.description:
The complete set of periods one version is in force for (D140).

It replaces the version's current declarations: periods not listed are
retracted and new ones are declared, atomically. An empty set is allowed
and leaves the version with no in-force period; the document keeps its
declared effective time.
EffectivePeriodsRequest.title: EffectivePeriodsRequest

EffectivePeriodsSet.description: What replacing one version's declared periods left in force.
EffectivePeriodsSet.title: EffectivePeriodsSet

EffectiveTimeCleared.description:
What leaving effective time did to one document (D140).

Every live declaration of the document is retracted and, when it had
declared effective time, the document returns to "the newest processed
version is current" for every reader believing after ``cleared_at``.
EffectiveTimeCleared.title: EffectiveTimeCleared

EvidenceSpan.description: One half-open supporting range on the selected occurrence (D119).
EvidenceSpan.title: EvidenceSpan

GraphInvocation.description: One graph helper's terminal work and truncation disclosure.
GraphInvocation.title: GraphInvocation

HistoryReadTime.description: Every text in force at any instant up to now.
HistoryReadTime.title: HistoryReadTime

IssuedKey.description: The key a successful device grant returns, with what the client stores.
IssuedKey.title: IssuedKey

IssuerMetadata.description: The fields of the issuer's authorization-server metadata the client uses.
IssuerMetadata.title: IssuerMetadata

KeyClaims.description:
The claims of a signed key, read **without verifying the signature**.

Only for routing and display: the engine perimeter verifies every key.
KeyClaims.title: KeyClaims

MatchingEdition.description:
One candidate edition of a periodised document that matched (D140 §3.5).

``version_id`` with ``representation_id`` is the ``source_open`` handle
that opens exactly this edition.
MatchingEdition.title: MatchingEdition

NamedReferenceTarget.description: The target exactly as the source names it (source content).
NamedReferenceTarget.title: NamedReferenceTarget

OverlapReadTime.description: Text in force at any instant of an inclusive window.
OverlapReadTime.title: OverlapReadTime

PendingRevocation.description: One replaced key whose revocation the issuer has not yet confirmed.
PendingRevocation.title: PendingRevocation

PendingRevocations.description: Every key still awaiting revocation, oldest first.
PendingRevocations.title: PendingRevocations

QueryErrorCode.description: Every public failure code, exactly as bound in design §4.1.
QueryErrorCode.title: QueryErrorCode

ReferenceGeneration.description:
One production of a version's references (D140 §6.1).

Rows of a generation are visible only while it is ``active``; a version
has at most one active generation per origin. A supplied generation is
``pending`` until the E0 crossref worker validates and activates it,
``rejected`` (with ``errors``) when it names an unknown source section,
and ``superseded`` once a later PUT or generation replaced it.
ReferenceGeneration.title: ReferenceGeneration

ReferenceGenerations.description: A version's reference generations, newest first.
ReferenceGenerations.title: ReferenceGenerations

ReferenceInput.description:
One line of a supplied NDJSON reference set (D140 §6.3).

``from_section_key`` is the section of the source version the reference
is made from (omitted: the whole document). A ``pinned`` reference names
the target's ``version_key``. ``amends`` must say whether its date is
known: ``change_date_known = true`` with ``change_effective_from``, or
``false`` without it; other kinds carry neither.
ReferenceInput.title: ReferenceInput

ReferenceItemError.description: Why one item of a reference set was rejected.
ReferenceItemError.title: ReferenceItemError

ReferenceTarget.description:
The document a supplied reference points at, named by its source identity.

``source_kind``/``source_ref`` are the target lineage's identity (the
values it was or will be ingested with), so a reference may name a
document that is not ingested yet. ``version_key`` pins one version
(with ``binding = pinned``); ``section_key`` names a section, else the
whole document.
ReferenceTarget.title: ReferenceTarget

ReferenceWindow.description:
A time window: from ``from`` (inclusive; null = unbounded) to ``until``.

``until`` is exclusive unless ``until_inclusive`` (an instant window has
``from == until`` and ``until_inclusive = true``); null is unbounded.
ReferenceWindow.title: ReferenceWindow

ReferencesSet.description:
What one ``PUT …/references`` did.

``outcome``: ``created`` — a new generation was recorded (``pending``,
or ``rejected`` when the version's structure already showed an unknown
source section); ``unchanged`` — the body equals the version's current
intent (a retry); ``pending_cancelled`` — the body equals the active
set, so the newer pending generation was cancelled. ``generation`` is
the generation the caller's intent now names.
ReferencesSet.title: ReferencesSet

ResolvedProject.description: The issuer's answer: which deployment serves one project for this key.
ResolvedProject.title: ResolvedProject

ResultColumn.description: One projected column: name, SQL type, nullability.
ResultColumn.title: ResultColumn

ResultLimits.description: The caps this request actually ran under.
ResultLimits.title: ResultLimits

SavedQuerySummary.description: Exact wire contract for one saved-query discovery row.
SavedQuerySummary.title: _SavedQuerySummary

ScopePending.description: Documents whose in-force text for the scope is still processing (D140 §3.7).
ScopePending.title: ScopePending

SectionAmendment.description: One live ``amends`` reference that targets the keyed section.
SectionAmendment.title: SectionAmendment

SectionHistoryPage.description:
A page of ``section_history`` rows.

Rows are ordered by effective start for a lineage with declared effective
periods (``periodised``) and by ``version_no`` otherwise. ``amendments``
is filled on the first page only. ``cursor`` pins ``evaluated_at`` and
``believed_at`` for the following pages.
SectionHistoryPage.title: SectionHistoryPage

SectionHistoryRow.description:
One selected version of the lineage and what it holds under the key.

``status``: ``present`` (``section`` is set), ``absent`` (the version is
indexed and lacks the key — a removed section), ``not_indexed`` (its
sections predate section keys and are not backfilled yet, so absence
cannot be told) or ``processing`` (the version is not readable yet).
SectionHistoryRow.title: SectionHistoryRow

SectionHistorySection.description: The keyed section as one version holds it.
SectionHistorySection.title: SectionHistorySection

SemanticInvocation.description: One §3.4 nomination invocation's disclosure (populated by Batch C).
SemanticInvocation.title: SemanticInvocation

StoredCredentials.description:
``credentials.json`` version 2: one key.

- An **issuer key** (``remember login``): ``issuer`` and ``key`` are set,
  ``api_url`` is not — the engine is resolved from the key.
- A **self-hosted entry** (``remember setup --self-hosted``): ``api_url``
  is set, ``issuer`` is not, and ``key`` is the engine's shared secret (or
  absent for an engine without authentication).

``extra="forbid"``: this program writes the file, so an unknown field is
corruption, and "run ``remember login``" is a recoverable answer.
StoredCredentials.title: StoredCredentials

TemporalMatch.description: Whether a fact definitely or possibly overlapped the query window.
TemporalMatch.title: TemporalMatch

TokenResponse.description: The token response (RFC 6749 §5.1) plus the issuer's non-secret extras.
TokenResponse.title: _TokenResponse
